context.objective: Document how we carry out Quarterly GP Workbook Production, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Thanks for sharing. Give me a moment to digest the file. Then I’ll follow up with a question.

The procedure says the preparer verifies the period, version and approval before copying the prior-period workbook and reconciling carried-forward amounts. Does that reflect how quarterly GP workbook production is done today?

Yes, that matches. As preparer I only start once the fund workbook for the same period is final and client-approved; if it is not, I stop and the fund team and client have to get us the approved source - no allocating, posting or output until then. If opening balances or previously recorded carry do not reconcile, I also stop until the difference is resolved with the reviewer and accounting. After that page, the next thing I do is review changes: I go through the governing documents first, then the Activities and Tax Activities tabs, record and validate every changed term, independently recalculate the affected results, and map every GP category to the fund workbook and confirm the amounts agree exactly. If a tab or document shows an unsupported or conflicting change, I stop the affected calculation and get a current interpretation from the governing document, the client or the adviser - the tab itself never decides the treatment - then recalculate what is affected. Then I confirm the capital and carry allocation levels, changes, effective dates, accounting tags, field mappings and schedule versions, the client confirms, and I lock the approved input set.
Once you lock the approved input set, what happens next to the workbook, and who receives it?

It stays with me for the calculations. First I run the capital allocation: apply the approved totality, deal or tranche method, identify the records for realized events, and reconcile member allocations to the GP capital total. Then I calculate carry from inception through the current period for each component and schedule, apply changes, combine the results and subtract carry already recorded - that gives the current-period entry; we never calculate carry for the current period alone. If accounting tags, included records, the allocation method or a schedule are missing or unreliable, I stop the affected allocation and get corrected data or an approved mapping from the client or the upstream teams; I do not infer a formula. Once calculations are complete, the calculation and journal entry support go to the Controller for review before posting. Then the approved entry is posted, the workbook is updated from the posted records, and the entry, workbook and source are reconciled. Who exactly posts the entry and who has authority to approve before posting is not confirmed, so I cannot tell you that.
After the entry, workbook and source are reconciled, what observable condition tells you production is complete, and where does the finished workbook go?

After that reconciliation the completed workbook goes to the Controller, with a Director as required, for the completed-workbook review. They review the trigger, changes, source ties, allocations, schedules, entry, statements and outputs, every comment has to be resolved, and then the final version is locked. If a source, posted entry, formula, schedule or review changes the workbook, output stops, all affected reconciliations are rerun and the final posted version is approved again - an earlier version cannot be used for output. From the final locked workbook we produce the outputs through whatever delivery method is implemented for that client - configured report, mail merge, workbook, PDF, GPES or portal. We validate field mapping, included records, totals, member details and the template, reconcile the outputs to the locked workbook at total and member level, obtain approval, release the client package and keep the release record. If a configured report is unavailable or GPES or the portal has not been validated, we stop until an approved, implemented fallback method is available, then reconcile and review that output the same way. It is complete when the validated client package is released with a saved release approval record and all sources, calculations, review and release records are saved. Who the release approver is has not been established, and whether the client must approve the GP workbook or output depends on the engagement and is not fully defined, so I do not know those.
What does the completed GP workbook help its recipients do?
